about.title: Three generations of Italian cooking
paragraphs: Bella Italia started as a small family kitchen serving neighbours on weekends. Today we still cook the same way: simple ingredients, patient sauces and pasta rolled by hand.
Our menu draws on the regional cooking of Naples, Bologna and Tuscany. We change the specials with the seasons so there is always something new to try alongside the classics.

about.title: Food from our grandmothers' kitchens
paragraphs: Kalinga Kitchen opened in 1998 with a single idea: serve the food Odia families eat at home, without shortcuts. Our dalma simmers for hours, our pakhala is fermented overnight and our sweets follow the temple recipes of Puri.
Every dish is cooked in earthen and brass vessels with mustard oil, panch phutana and ingredients bought each morning from the Unit 1 market.

image.alt: Friends sharing dishes across a table

chef.name: Sulochana Mohanty
chef.title: Founder & Head Cook
chef.quote: Odia food is patient food. You cannot rush a dalma, and you should not try.
chef.bio: Sulochana learned to cook in her family home in Cuttack and has led the Kalinga Kitchen stove for twenty-five years.

about.title: Slow food from the royal kitchens
paragraphs: Dum pukht cooking seals the pot with dough and lets time do the work. At Saffron Court every biryani, korma and nihari is cooked this way, for hours, so the spices settle into something quiet and deep.
The dining room is dressed in brass, velvet and candlelight. Service is unhurried. We ask only that you give the evening the time it deserves.

about.title: Everything tastes better over a real fire
paragraphs: Ember & Oak started with a single wood-fired grill and a stubborn belief that smoke and char make food better. We still cook on oak and mango wood, and we still cut our own steaks.
The room is relaxed on purpose. Come in work clothes or dressed up, share a platter at the long table, or sit at the bar and let the team pick your drink.

about.title: A little of Santorini, above Saheed Nagar
paragraphs: Blanco Kitchen & Terrace brings the white walls, blue doors and bougainvillea of the Greek islands to a rooftop in Saheed Nagar. Inside, a garden ceiling hangs over the dining hall; outside, the terrace is made for long evenings.

The menu travels just as far: cheesy pizzas and baked lasagna, Indian kebabs and biryani, Oriental mains in your choice of sauce, and a long list of mocktails and shakes. Every dish is prepared fresh when you order.
